today_summary: GCM26 marked $4,114.40 on the 2026-11-10 session, the top of the 5-day range, with calls outvoting puts 10,952 to 5,636 in daily volume. The chain is structurally call-heavy — P/C OI 0.41, 292,142 call OI against 120,383 put OI — with the nearest resistance shelf at $4,200 (5,072 call OI) and the first real floor at $4,000 (4,973 put OI). ATM IV of 21.51% prices a 1σ daily move of just $55.75 (1.36%). Max pain sits at $5,225, but that is $1,110 above spot and driven by legacy call OI at $5,000–$5,500 — treat it as structural skew, not a magnet.
five_day_thesis: Spot has advanced $174.10 ($3,940.30 → $4,114.40, +4.4%) across the window while max pain barely moved (-$25 to $5,225) — this rally is price catching up to a long-standing call-heavy structure, not fresh upside positioning. The decisive change is the gamma regime: dealer net GEX flipped from -157.3 to +167.7 on 2026-11-05 and has stayed positive four straight sessions, now +305.1, converting dealers from vol amplifiers into vol dampeners. The put wall migrated down $200 ($3,900 → $3,700) on 2026-11-05 and has not moved since, so the downside bid was abandoned rather than reinforced — there is now air between spot and the heaviest put OI, with only the $4,000 shelf in between. The call wall has been pinned at $5,500 (16,615 OI) all five sessions, an unmoved ceiling that no longer reflects where flow is going: today's call volume concentrated at $4,400 (1,836) and $4,500 (1,761). ATM IV compressed 1.23pp (22.74% → 21.51%) through the entire advance — rising price on falling vol is the signature of a grind, not a breakout.
what_changed: GEX regime flipped negative (-157.3) to positive (+305.1) on 2026-11-05 and has held four sessions — dealer hedging now dampens moves
Put wall migrated $3,900 → $3,700 (-$200) and froze there, leaving the $4,000 shelf (4,973 OI) as the only near-spot floor
Spot gained $174.10 (+4.4%) to close the window at the top of its 5-day range, $4,114.40
ATM IV compressed 22.74% → 21.51% (-1.23pp), cutting the implied 1σ day to $55.75
Call volume hit a 5-day high of 10,952 contracts, clustered at $4,400 and $4,500 rather than at the static $5,500 wall
Max pain drifted just -$25 to $5,225 while spot rose $174 — the gap closed on price, not on repositioning
prediction: Bias is constructive but range-compressed above $4,100: positive dealer gamma (+305.1) plus 21.51% IV argues for a grind into the $4,200 call shelf (5,072 OI) rather than an impulse leg. Loss of $4,100 drops price into the negative net-gamma pocket spanning $4,075 down to $3,900 (-2.3 to -67.5), where hedging amplifies instead of cushions and a fast retest of the $4,000 put wall opens. Invalidation is a sustained break below $3,990.
